about: The answer to the one-line request of exercise 1, shown to participants as the starting point.
route: a Claude Code subagent given the request text as its whole prompt; the answer saved as returned
strengths: It apologises first for the one promise that was clearly broken: no delivery day was confirmed by Friday.
Its figures are right, and it does not promise the credit: it says the amount is the {managerRole}'s decision.
issues: It decides something nobody asked it to decide: "We will issue a corrected invoice that removes those cartons." That is not in the thread, and it is not what the policy says: missing goods are sent on the next delivery run (rule 2), so the cartons are still owed, not taken off the invoice.
It says "I have also sent her your receipt". Nobody has: in message 4, {staffFirst} sent the {managerRole} the photos and the request; the receipt arrived only in message 5.
It promises an answer "the same day" to any further e-mail. The policy asks for one working day (rule 7); a same-day promise is one the writer may not be able to keep.
It commits the {managerRole} to a decision by a date ("Dana will give you her decision by [date ...]"): a promise made on someone else's behalf.
It cannot be sent as it is: it has three gaps in square brackets, and formatting marks (the asterisks) that many e-mail programs would show as they are.

Its own notes under the line are useful, and incomplete. They flag the three gaps and say that nobody has agreed to the {money:creditAsked}, but say nothing about the corrected invoice or the receipt it claims was sent. They also work out a date the thread does not give ("14 March"): right by the calendar, but worked out, so check it.
